edges.description: The germline expanded allele is further expanded somatically across the lifespan and across tissues by aberrant mismatch repair.

edges.description: Ongoing somatic CTG expansion increases the expanded-CUG RNA burden that accumulates in nuclear foci, intensifying the RNA-toxicity cascade.

edges.description: Sustained expression of a repeat-length-stable CUG RNA drives progressive cardiac disease while MBNL-dependent splicing stays static, so at least one intermediate on this branch is not the spliceopathy and is not yet identified.
Large CTG expansions push DM1 muscle precursor cells into p16-dependent premature senescence rather than replicative exhaustion.
intermediate_mechanisms: A cellular stress attributable to the expanded repeat drives p16 accumulation; the step linking retained CUG RNA to p16 induction is uncharacterized.

nodes.description: Baliforsen (ISIS 598769) is an antisense oligonucleotide directed at DMPK mRNA, intended to lower the toxic CUG-repeat transcript at its source rather than treat a downstream symptom. It is investigational, not approved. In the completed multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 1/2a dose-escalation trial (NCT02312011, 48 dosed adults across five dose levels) it was generally well tolerated, with injection-site reactions, headache, contusion, and nausea the common adverse events and one case of transient thrombocytopenia. Muscle drug concentration rose with dose but stayed below the level predicted to achieve substantial target reduction, so this trial established tolerability and exposure without demonstrating target engagement. It should therefore not be cited as therapeutic corroboration of the RNA-toxicity mechanism; delivery to muscle is the limiting problem.

nodes.description: In DM1 heart tissue, MBNL-dependent spliceopathy shifts SCN5A from the adult exon 6B isoform toward the fetal exon 6A isoform. The resulting Nav1.5 channel has reduced excitability, providing a mutation-to-cardiac conduction defect branch in the pathograph. This branch contributes but is not sufficient: forcing the adult exon 6B isoform in a CUG960 DM1 heart model leaves conduction delay and structural change unimproved, so DM1 cardiac disease is not the sum of this splicing defect. See the Splicing-Independent Progressive Cardiac Pathology node for the parallel arm, and the dm1_nonsplicing_cardiac_progression discussion for what remains unresolved.

nodes.description: The DM1 CTG repeat lies near SIX5, and repeat-associated local chromatin or transcriptional effects can reduce SIX5 dosage. Mouse Six5 loss produces progressive ocular cataracts, supporting a parallel lens branch in addition to toxic RNA spliceopathy.

evidence.snippet: Our results demonstrate that the rate and severity of cataract formation is inversely related to Six5 dosage and is temporally progressive.

nodes.description: DM1 muscle precursor cells carrying large CTG expansions stop dividing early not because they have used up their replicative capacity but because they enter premature senescence. p16 accumulates abnormally, and abolishing p16 activity overcomes the early growth arrest and restores extended proliferation; accelerated telomere shortening, which is also present, does not account for the p16 induction. Because the reserve is arrested rather than exhausted, this is a candidate contributor to impaired regeneration and atrophy in large-expansion DM1 that is separable from the spliceopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Large CTG repeats trigger p16-dependent premature senescence in myotonic dystrophy type 1 muscle precursor cells.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that an abnormal accumulation of p16 is responsible for this defect because the abolition of p16 activity overcomes early growth arrest and restores an extended proliferative capacity.

nodes.description: Beyond the inherited germline expansion, the DMPK CTG repeat continues to expand somatically throughout life, driven by aberrant DNA mismatch repair (the MutSβ/MSH3 complex licenses expansion; FAN1 is protective). Somatic expansion is progressive with age and tissue-specific — largest in the most clinically affected tissues such as skeletal muscle — and its rate, set by the expression balance of DNA-repair modifiers, tracks disease severity and age of onset. This ongoing somatic expansion continually raises the expanded-CUG RNA burden that drives the downstream RNA-toxicity cascade.

evidence.reference_title: Somatic expansion behaviour of the (CTG)n repeat in myotonic dystrophy knock-in mice is differentially affected by Msh3 and Msh6 mismatch-repair proteins.
evidence.snippet: Introducing the (CTG)84 allele into an Msh3-deficient background completely blocked the somatic repeat instability.

evidence.reference_title: Tissue-specific CTG•CAG expansion rate and disease severity are modified by DNA repair genes expression levels in myotonic dystrophy type 1 patients.
evidence.snippet: higher FAN1 expression was associated with reduced somatic expansion and later onset.

nodes.description: Expanded CUG RNA sequesters MBNL family proteins in nuclear foci and is accompanied by increased CELF1/CUGBP1 activity in affected tissues. The resulting loss of adult MBNL activity and CELF1/MBNL imbalance causes fetal-pattern alternative splicing across skeletal muscle, heart, endocrine, and CNS transcripts.

evidence.reference_title: Myotonic disorders.
evidence.snippet: Mutant RNA sequesters MBNL1, a splice regulator protein and depletes MBNL1 from the nucleoplasm. Loss of MBNL1 results in altered splicing of ClC-1 mRNA.

evidence.reference_title: Splicing misregulation of SCN5A contributes to cardiac-conduction delay and heart arrhythmia in myotonic dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: The pathogenesis of DM involves a RNA gain-of-function mechanism caused by expression of mutant RNAs containing hundred to thousands of CUG or CCUG repeats that interfere with the splicing of other pre-mRNAs through dysfunction of two classes of RNA-binding proteins.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptional and post-transcriptional impact of toxic RNA in myotonic dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: We found that the majority of changes induced by CUG(exp) RNA in skeletal muscle can be explained by reduced activity of Mbnl1, including many changes that are secondary to myotonia.

evidence.reference_title: Increased steady-state levels of CUGBP1 in myotonic dystrophy 1 are due to PKC-mediated hyperphosphorylation.
evidence.snippet: Activation of PKC is required for CUGBP1 hyperphosphorylation in DM1 cells, and PKCalpha and betaII directly phosphorylate CUGBP1 in vitro.

evidence.reference_title: Alternative splicing dysregulation secondary to skeletal muscle regeneration.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, CELF1 was elevated in nuclei of mature myofibers of the DM1 model, consistent with a primary effect of pathogenic RNA expression.

nodes.description: Cardiac disease in DM1 worsens over time through a route that does not run through the MBNL-dependent spliceopathy. In an inducible heart-specific model expressing a stable, interrupted 960-CUG-repeat RNA — a design that holds repeat length fixed and so excludes somatic expansion — sustained expression produced progressive cardiac enlargement, contractile dysfunction, conduction delay, myocardial fibrosis, and reduced survival while MBNL-dependent splicing defects stayed static. Suppressing the transgene rescued the cardiac abnormalities, but reversibility fell with longer exposure, implying a component that accumulates rather than simply tracking the current RNA burden. The intermediate steps between persistent nuclear CUG RNA and fibrotic and contractile failure are not identified.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive cardiac phenotypes and reduced reversibility from long-term CUGexp RNA expression in a DM1 mouse model.
evidence.snippet: Sustained CUGexp RNA expression caused progressive cardiac enlargement, contractile dysfunction, conduction delay, myocardial fibrosis, and reduced survival, while MBNL-dependent splicing defects remained static, consistent with the stable repeat length.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive cardiac phenotypes and reduced reversibility from long-term CUGexp RNA expression in a DM1 mouse model.
evidence.snippet: Suppression of CUGexp RNA expression rescued cardiac abnormalities, but reversibility declined with longer exposure to the toxic RNA.

evidence.reference_title: Rescue of Scn5a mis-splicing does not improve the structural and functional heart defects of a DM1 heart mouse model.
evidence.snippet: We showed that correction Scn5a mis-splicing does not improve the DM1 heart conduction delays and structural changes induced by CUG repeat RNA expression.

nodes.description: The expanded DMPK repeat is transcribed into CUG repeat-containing RNA that is retained in the nucleus and recruits RNA-binding proteins that normally regulate adult splicing programs. Nuclear retention, rather than the higher-order focus itself, is the toxic state: quantitative imaging in patient-derived myotubes shows that most objects scored as "foci" are single RNA molecules, and that these individual nuclear-retained transcripts titrate MBNL1. Multimeric foci arise from transcriptional bursting, dissociate over time, and depend on MBNL proteins for their own assembly, so they are better read as a marker of the retained-RNA burden than as the pathogenic species.

evidence.reference_title: Myotonic syndromes.
evidence.snippet: In both types of myotonic dystrophy the expanded repeat is transcribed and the RNA produced from the mutant allele is retained in nuclear inclusions. Recent studies suggest that the mutant RNA has a toxic effect on muscle fibers by interfering with the essential functions of the myonucleus, such as RNA processing.

evidence.reference_title: Myotonic dystrophy: RNA pathogenesis comes into focus.
evidence.snippet: the clinical features common to both diseases are caused by a gain-of-function RNA mechanism in which the CUG and CCUG repeats alter cellular function, including alternative splicing of various genes.

evidence.reference_title: DM1 repeat-expanded RNAs confer RNA toxicity as individual nuclear-retained RNAs.
evidence.snippet: Altogether, these observations argue that the persistence of nuclear-retained CUG RNAs, independent of higher-order RNA assemblies, titrates MBNL1 and contributes to disease progression.

nodes.description: Transcription of the expanded repeat produces double-stranded RNA in DM cells, and lens tissue from DM1 and DM2 cataracts carries a shared transcriptional signature dominated by interferon-regulated genes and dsRNA-response genes, with 83 percent of dysregulated genes common to the two diseases. This is a candidate lens mechanism sitting outside the MBNL1/CELF1 splicing axis. It is an expression association in surgical specimens: no perturbation was performed, there is no MBNL1 comparison arm, and the signature has not been shown to precede or cause opacity, so its weight relative to the SIX5 locus branch is unresolved.
nodes.id: dsRNA-Triggered Innate Immune Activation in Lens

evidence.reference_title: Activation of the innate immune response and interferon signalling in myotonic dystrophy type 1 and type 2 cataracts.
evidence.snippet: The upregulated genes in DM1 and DM2 were highly enriched in both interferon-regulated genes (IRGs) and genes associated with the response to dsRNA and the innate immune response.
